result:
Users with no thread follow-up setting are now prompted when they reply without tagging PostHog. I didn't run any tests, per your instructions, so none of this has been run.

**What happens now**
- **Webhook gate:** `resolve_untagged_followup_mode` in `slack_settings.py` now returns `None` when the person never chose. That used to mean "never", which made the webhook drop the reply. Now it passes through to the workflow. Users who already chose `auto`, `ask` or `never` behave exactly as before.
- **Prompt:** the existing confirmation activity (`request_untagged_followup_confirmation_activity`) now treats "unset" like `ask` and posts the "send this to the agent?" prompt. It still runs only after the classifier judges the reply worth forwarding. I did not touch the workflow itself, so there is no Temporal versioning concern.
- **Saving a default:** when the replier is the thread creator and has no setting, the prompt has two extra buttons: "Always pick up my follow-ups" and "Never pick up follow-ups". "Always" also sends the current message. "Never" dismisses it. Both save the choice through `save_untagged_followup_mode_if_unset`, which never overwrites an existing choice. The handlers check that the person clicking is the one the prompt was for.
- **Non-creators:** someone replying in another person's thread still gets the plain prompt with no save buttons, since the setting belongs to the thread creator.
- **Home tab:** the "Thread follow-ups" card now always shows. With no stored value the picker has no preselected option and a placeholder of "Ask me each time". Picking a value there saves it through the existing handler.

**Tests**
I adjusted the existing tests for the new "unset" meaning and added an "unset" case to the activity test. That covers the settings resolver, the webhook routing, the home card and the confirmation activity. I added no tests for the new "Always" and "Never" save buttons or for `save_untagged_followup_mode_if_unset`, so that path is unexercised.

The main changes are in `products/slack_app/backend/api.py` (the prompt buttons and click handlers) and `products/slack_app/backend/services/slack_settings.py`.
